course.title: Food Safety for Small-Scale Produce Growers
course.college: College of Agriculture (sample course for testing)
course.audience: Small farm owners, market garden managers, and extension volunteers; no science background assumed
course.delivery: Online, self-paced, on-demand (converted from a live cohort syllabus)
course.description: Learners identify food safety hazards on a produce farm and put practical controls in place, finishing with a one-page farm food safety plan.

outcomes.statement: Explain how pathogens reach fresh produce and why produce eaten raw carries higher risk.
Assess agricultural water sources and choose an appropriate testing and treatment approach.
Apply safe handling practices for raw manure and compost on a small farm.
Design worker hygiene, harvest, and cleaning practices that reduce contamination.
Create a written farm food safety plan with records an inspector would accept.

units.title: Why produce safety matters
units.summary: Learners see why produce eaten raw carries risk, meet the pathogens that matter on a farm, and trace the five routes contamination travels.

objectives.statement: Explain why fresh produce has no kill step between the field and the plate.
Identify the bacteria and viruses most often linked to produce outbreaks and where each comes from.
Trace the five routes of contamination on your own farm.

topics.title: Why produce eaten raw is different
The pathogens that matter on a farm

activities.title: Walk your farm
activities.type: guided field observation with model answer
activities.where: In the package; notes carry into the final plan

sources: week1-pathogens-and-routes.pptx, slides 1 to 4 and speaker notes

units.title: Water, soil amendments, and animals
units.summary: Learners rank water sources by risk, read a water test result, handle manure and compost safely, and decide what to do when animals get into a field.

objectives.statement: Rank agricultural water sources by contamination risk and justify the ranking.
Interpret a generic E. coli water test result and decide on a next step.
Apply raw manure and compost handling practices, including application intervals and storage.
Decide whether produce near animal intrusion can be harvested.

activities.title: Water source assessment worksheet
activities.where: Brief in the package; submit in the Brightspace assignment folder

sources: week2-water-and-amendments.pptx, slides 1 to 4 and speaker notes

units.title: Workers, harvest, and packing
units.summary: Learners set worker health and hygiene rules, plan a field handwashing station, and set safe harvest and packing practices.

objectives.statement: Set an illness reporting rule and a training plan for every worker, family and volunteers included.
Plan a handwashing station that meets the course guideline for supplies and distance.
Apply harvest container and packing area practices that prevent contamination.

activities.title: Plan your handwashing station
activities.type: self-check with model answer (replaces the live discussion)
activities.where: Brief in the package; submit a photo or sketch in the Brightspace assignment folder

sources: photo-visitor-rules-sign.jpg, read by OCR (visitor rules for topic 3.3)

units.title: Cleaning, records, and your farm plan
units.summary: Learners separate cleaning from sanitizing, keep the records an inspector expects, and write their farm food safety plan.

objectives.statement: Distinguish cleaning from sanitizing and sequence them correctly.
Keep cleaning, water, and training records in a form an inspector would accept.
Write a one-page farm food safety plan for your operation.

topics.title: Write your farm food safety plan

activities.title: Farm food safety plan
activities.type: final project with template and rubric
activities.where: Brief in the package; submit in the Brightspace assignment folder

sources: scanned-handout-sanitation-log.pdf, pages 1 and 2, read by OCR (what to log daily and common mistakes, for topic 4.2)

conversion_notes: The syllabus is written for a live cohort. The Week 3 Zoom discussion on handwashing stations becomes a self-check with a model answer (Activity 3). Lost: peer feedback on each station. Faculty should confirm the self-check meets the objective.
Peer review of the final plan on the discussion board is replaced by a rubric and a worked example. Faculty should decide whether a graded instructor review is still offered.
Week numbers and due dates were removed from module titles so the course can run on demand.

gaps.needed_for: Module 01, topic 1.3 and media item M01-V02
